inlines.text: Anthropic 今天登陆公开市场，此次 IPO 有望为公司及其投资者募集数十亿美元。但最大的意外或许是，其中很大一部分资金最终会流向作为供应商的投资者。

blocks.text: 亚马逊和谷歌是 Anthropic 最大的两家基础设施合作伙伴，按公司最新 IPO 价格每股 83 美元计算，两家持股合计价值约 3079 亿美元。根据 Anthropic IPO 招股书披露的持股数据，亚马逊向这家 AI 初创公司投资了 180 亿美元，其 14.7% 的持股价值将超过 1590 亿美元；谷歌 13.7% 的持股价值则接近 1490 亿美元。

blocks.text: 自 2023 年以来，谷歌已向 Anthropic 投资 123 亿美元，另有承诺的 300 亿美元取决于 Anthropic 能否达成某些业绩里程碑。除台积电外，Anthropic 还宣布与英伟达、AMD、博通、微软、美光科技等其他基础设施供应商投资者达成数十亿美元的战略合作，Anthropic 将向这些公司采购产品。

blocks.text: 这就是让一些观察人士对 AI 热潮深表怀疑的循环融资。这些公司不仅是投资者，也是 Anthropic 最大的供应商。表面上看，亚马逊和谷歌向 Anthropic 投入了数十亿美元，但当 Anthropic 需要训练模型或为用户运行 Claude 时，这笔钱又原路流回它们手中。从远处看，这像是云公司前所未有的营收增长，以及 Anthropic 前所未有的融资规模——但实际上，只是同一笔钱从一个口袋转到另一个口袋。

blocks.text: “这笔持股非常值得，这些公司也不再需要（供应商）提供更多支持了，”Brookhart 对 TechCrunch 表示。“亚马逊不需要再扶持他们了。收入全都来自其他客户。”

blocks.text: 不过，这并不意味着服务器账单会减少。根据一份监管文件，Anthropic 已承诺支出 9000 亿美元，主要用于算力和基础设施。部分协议设有终止条款，但 Brookhart 认为公司有足够实力付清这些款项。

blocks.text: 在两位分析师看来，Anthropic 最大的风险就是输掉 AI 竞赛。目前，公司的增长得益于它处于生成式 AI 的前沿——但如果被 OpenAI、Google DeepMind，甚至廉价的开源权重模型超越，情况可能迅速改变。正如 Luria 所说：“如果我们都在用别人的模型，那 Anthropic 就不值 1.5 万亿美元，而是一文不值。”

blocks.text: Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the company and its investors. But the biggest surprise may be just how much of that money will end up going to supplier-investors.

inlines.text: Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the company and its investors. But the biggest surprise may be just how much of that money will end up going to supplier-investors.

blocks.text: Amazon and Google, two of Anthropic’s largest infrastructure partners, hold stakes valued around a combined $307.9 billion at the company’s updated IPO price of $83 per share. Amazon, which invested $18 billion into the AI startup, would see its 14.7% stake hit upwards of $159 billion, while Google’s 13.7% stake is valued at nearly $149 billion, according to share ownership figures disclosed in Anthropic’s IPO prospectus.

blocks.text: A handful of other AI infrastructure providers are also positioned to benefit. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC have joined Google in committing $26 billion to Anthropic at its IPO price in a private placement.

blocks.text: In total, Google has invested $12.3 billion into Anthropic since 2023, with another promised $30 billion dependent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones. And with the exception of TSMC, Anthropic has announced multi-billion-dollar strategic partnerships with its other infrastructure supplier investors — including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, and Micron — that would see Anthropic purchasing their products.

blocks.text: This is the circular financing that has made some observers so skeptical of the AI boom. These companies are not just investors; they’re also Anthropic’s biggest suppliers. It might look like Amazon and Google are putting billions into Anthropic, but they get that money right back when Anthropic needs to train a model or serve Claude to users. From afar, it looks like unprecedented revenue growth for cloud companies and unprecedented fundraising from Anthropic — but it’s just the same money passing from one pocket to another.

blocks.text: Today’s IPO marks a critical change in that financing system, the moment it might just become self-sustaining. Those investments appear to have paid off, and are now liquid. Anthropic is still operating at a net loss of tens of billions of dollars each quarter — but it will no longer be suppliers and private investors footing the bill. Now, capital will come from a mix of public-market investors and corporate bonds, neither of which have the conflicts-of-interest that caused concerns before.

blocks.text: For both analysts, the biggest risk to Anthropic is simply that it will lose the AI race. Right now, the company’s growth is fueled by its status at the frontier of generative AI — but if it’s overtaken by OpenAI, Google DeepMind, or even cheap open-weight models, that could change fast. As Luria put it: “If we’re all using other people’s models, then Anthropic’s not worth a trillion and a half dollars. It’s worth nothing.”
